title: Etale descent and coherent geometry of normalized-word maximum centers
statement:
Over $\mathbf Q$, let $X\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed embedding with $X$ reduced and $P$ smooth, separated and of finite type [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix the simultaneous normalized word assignment of [lem-trf-normalized-resolution-word-gluing]: $w_H(x)=\bot$ at regular points and $w_H(x)=(A_x,t_x)$ otherwise, where $A_x=(c_x,\Delta^{q_x}h_x)$ is the normalized local Hilbert--Samuel head and $t_x$ is the marked-ideal word with its leading $1$ removed. Let $H$ be any finite admissible history for this assignment [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history]. Suppose its current ambient scheme $P_H$ is smooth, separated and of finite type and its strict transform $X_H$ is reduced. If $X_H$ is nonregular, let $m>\bot$ be the greatest value of $w_H$ and put $T=\{x:w_H(x)=m\}$.

The reduced induced closed subscheme $M=T_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X_H$ is nonempty and regular [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, def-weil-regular-scheme]. More precisely, on etale neighbourhoods carrying the local Hilbert--Samuel presentations, its scheme-theoretic pullback is the smooth full-maximum center of the presenting marked-ideal word; these local centers have normal crossings with the ordered exceptional data [def-weil-etale-morphism, lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-local-presentations, lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine]. The closed set $T$ meets no regular point and contains no irreducible component of $X_H$; in particular it contains no nonempty open subset. The ideals defining $M$ in both $X_H$ and $P_H$ are coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. The local center identifications concern the reduced ideal structures, not only their underlying point sets.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11, p.93; etale descent of the full maximum center, old step 3 and the Noetherian coherence part of step 4. Supporting Stacks Tags 02GO (morphisms.tex lemma-base-change-etale), 033B (algebra.tex lemma-reduced-goes-up), 00FN (algebra.tex lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00FP (algebra.tex lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation).

proof.text: The current ambient is locally Noetherian by its finite-type map to Spec Q [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its closed strict transform and all reduced closed subschemes are locally Noetherian by quotient permanence [def-weil-closed-immersion, lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]. A nonregular stage therefore has a point with nonregular stalk. The finite image, closed upper levels and bottom characterization in [lem-trf-normalized-resolution-word-gluing] give a greatest attained value m strictly above bottom. Its equality set is the closed m-upper level. The reduced induced structure is nonempty by its range formula [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme].

Apply [lem-trf-resolution-word-local-maximum-models] to this specified m and T. The resulting local extensions give exactly the required reduced smooth normal-crossings centers and cartesian squares. The final intrinsic map is etale since it is the chart etale map composed with the isomorphism transporting its last index [def-weil-etale-morphism].

For any z in the reduced center use the range formula to put its image in T. A chart supplied by the preceding step contains a specified lift of that image: the pointed-chart equation, followed by the final-index transport, is the identity stage map. Surjectivity of scheme points onto a fiber product gives a point w of the local smooth center mapping to z. The map from that center to the reduced global center is etale by base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], hence flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Its source is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. On stalks apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular], using the already established local Noetherianity of the target. Thus the global center is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme].

Mathlib isField_stalk_of_closure_mem_irreducibleComponents says directly that every component generic stalk of a reduced scheme is a field, hence regular. The bottom characterization and positivity of m exclude these points from T. Each component contains its generic point, so none is contained in T. Generic points are dense (Mathlib genericPoints.closure); hence the complement of T is dense and the interior of T is empty. This replaces the detour through the Serre criterion.

For every ideal sheaf on a locally Noetherian scheme the adopted source library already proves Scheme.Modules.isQuasicoherent_toModules and Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_toModules in Modules.HilbertPolynomial. In particular both the intrinsic vanishing ideal and the kernel of its composite immersion into the ambient scheme are quasi-coherent and finite type. The equivalence [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] proves their coherence directly.

Statement, source and blueprint are unchanged from the Q153 snapshot; the dropped stmt_deps (nagata blowup and strict transform) reach the statement through def-trf-admissible-embedded-history, accepted as advisory. Steps checked against each cited statement. (1) P_H is Noetherian as finite type over Spec Q (01T6) and quotients stay Noetherian (00FN). (2) Finite image, closed upper level sets and bottom only at regular points (gluing statement) give a greatest m>bottom and a nonempty closed T disjoint from the regular locus. (3) Removing larger heads by upper semicontinuity and comparing the engine word (1,t_y) with the global maximum makes the engine's full maximum set exactly the preimage of T; the engine gives a smooth center with normal crossings, with no termination used. (4) Reduced pullback along etale maps (first clause of lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent), C_a reduced, and the factorization through U by vanishing in reduced rings give scheme equality through reduced-induced uniqueness, also in P_H. (5) The smooth center is regular, the etale base change is flat, both stalks are Noetherian, and flat-under-regular (00OF) gives M regular. (6) Serre reduced implies R_0 (031R) puts generic points outside T; the open-set argument is right. (7) Ideals are quasi-coherent, of finite type and coherent (01XZ) in X_H and P_H. ILO VIII 2.3.11 (p.93) and 2.3.12(ii) (p.94) were read: regular centers in the singular locus; proof_origin agent with BMT WANTED is correct. Small cases checked: empty or regular X_H, node xy=0, a chart missing T, point components. No new nodes and no cycle (1519-node walk); the one missing id is deep in the base closure, not from this delivery. No SGA. The six declared tool_uses are generic and accepted.
